selection_rationale: Candidate-7f4a (verifier‑anchored generate–validate–repair) most directly addresses the identified gap CG1—integrating LLM proposals with a formal network‑change verifier (Relational NetKAT) and a bounded repair loop—while being experimentally falsifiable, feasible within the stated resource envelope, and tightly aligned with the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track. Key supporting records show verifier methods and generate–validate–repair promise and feasibility.
unresolved_uncertainties: Verifier expressiveness and concrete false‑negative/false‑positive rates on the chosen safety properties for the task set (scalability/generalization to production‑scale topologies).
Repair‑loop convergence behavior: which error classes fail to converge within the 3‑iteration budget and how often.
Semantic correctness vs syntactic fixes: model repairs may appear syntactically plausible yet remain semantically incorrect for operational policies.
End‑to‑end latency and variability (retrieval/model/verifier/repair) and whether it meets real‑time operator budgets.
Representativeness and realism of the public intent→configuration task set and risk of design bias from synthetic/topology choices.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Enumerate and document the verifier‑encoded safety properties; add explicit tests to estimate verifier false‑negative and false‑positive rates on held‑out cases and outline verifier limitations.

Specify the repair prompting protocol: exact repair prompt templates, instruction framing, temperature and seed policies, allowed prompt length, and an explicit stopping/no‑improvement rule for repairs.
Define latency budgets and measurement protocol: decompose latency (model, verifier, repair iterations), preregister caps (e.g., 1s/3s/10s), and plan for repeated runs to quantify variability.
Publish the intent→configuration dataset, seeds, all prompts, and pairing rules; include provenance checks to ensure no pre‑lock experimental data were used and enable external reproducibility.

Add mitigation checks for semantic correctness: define secondary semantic validators or oracle checks (where available) and a qualitative failure‑mode taxonomy to capture syntactically plausible but semantically wrong repairs.
